theme: Awesome lists and curated catalogues: awesome-public-datasets, awesome-alternative-data, awesome-quant data, awesome-economics, awesome-tourism, awesome-real-estate, awesome-transportation-data

candidates.name: awesome-public-datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: 78.9k-star topic-centric meta-list (MIT) of open datasets across ~30 categories including Social Sciences, Economics, Transportation, Real Estate, Government; each entry is a link out (data.gov, Eurostat, etc.), not a hosted file. Updated same-day (14 Sep 2026), very actively PR'd.
candidates.why_useful: Fastest way to sweep for a free source we have not seen yet on gaps 6-13 (regional travel volume, hotel supply, housing/rental, consumer spend); worth a targeted re-read of its Transportation/Economics/Real-Estate sections rather than a full dataset in itself.
candidates.size_hint: README index only, no data files in this repo

candidates.name: apd-core
candidates.what_it_holds: Machine-readable CSV backing store for awesome-public-datasets, organized as one CSV per category (e.g. core/Transportation.csv) with dataset name/url/description columns; source-of-truth for new dataset PRs to the main list.
candidates.why_useful: Lets a future pass query the whole awesome-public-datasets index programmatically (e.g. filter Transportation.csv, Economics.csv) instead of scraping the rendered README; the Transportation.csv category file was confirmed present via GitHub contents API on 14 Sep 2026 (fetch of raw file 404'd, likely a path/branch mismatch worth revisiting).
candidates.size_hint: one CSV per top-level category, small

candidates.name: awesome-alternative-data
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated alt-data list for investment research (updated 7 Sep 2026) with sections Property/Real Estate, Consumer Spending & Transactions, Web Traffic & Engagement, Macroeconomic Data. Concrete free entries: HM Land Registry Price Paid (every England/Wales residential sale since 1995, free, point-in-time by construction), Dubai Pulse DLD transaction history (free); paid entries: Earnest Analytics, Consumer Edge, Second Measure/Bloomberg, Fable Data (card/transaction panels), Similarweb & Semrush (web traffic/engagement APIs).
candidates.why_useful: HM Land Registry and Dubai Pulse are free, long-run, point-in-time housing-transaction feeds relevant to STR-vs-LTR host economics (gap 13); the Similarweb/Semrush and card-panel entries map directly to gaps 5 (engagement) and 6 (consumer spend) even though most require paid access, useful as a sourcing map.

candidates.name: awesome-real-estate-apis
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated list of real-estate APIs and data sources by country (official government open data, commercial, scraping-based), sibling repo to the alt-data list above.
candidates.why_useful: Country-by-country index for sourcing housing/rental comps to test STR<->LTR crossover (gap 13) beyond the Zillow/Redfin/HUD sources already known.

candidates.name: awesome-real-estate
candidates.what_it_holds: 369-star curated real-estate resource list (CC0), regularly updated (8 Sep 2026), with regional sections. Notable concrete data entries: BailleurVerif (MIT, open dataset of non-compliant French rental listings across 7 cities, ~210 listings/wave), Staying API (commercial real-time Airbnb/STR listing data by listing ID/address/dates/price, REST+MCP, free tier), Cost Segregation Benchmarks 2026 (CC-BY-4.0 CSV, 260 US studies), Phuket condo asking-price snapshot (CC BY 4.0, 391 listings CSV/JSON), Bangkok off-plan housing pipeline (CC BY 4.0, refreshed every 2 days), Japan Neighborhoods (free API, crime/safety/price for 5,078 Tokyo neighborhoods).
candidates.why_useful: 'Staying API' is a live, queryable Airbnb/STR pricing source with a free tier -- directly on-point for gap 2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs) if the free tier covers enough listings to sample; the small CC-BY regional snapshots (Phuket, Bangkok) are APAC/SE-Asia STR-adjacent supply signals not in our current holdings.
candidates.size_hint: README link list; individual linked datasets are small (hundreds of rows)
candidates.geography: France, US, Thailand, Thailand/Bangkok, Japan, global

candidates.name: awesome-real-estate-investing
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated collection of tools, platforms, and projects for real-estate investors/operators/agents; skews toward software/CRM tooling rather than raw data per its description.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal -- flagged for completeness but likely low signal-to-noise for data specifically; would need a manual README read to confirm any data-source sections.

candidates.name: awesome-economics
candidates.what_it_holds: 1,732-star curated collection of links for economists (data, journals, blogs, tools), actively updated (12 Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: Broad economist-curated index worth mining for regional/international statistical-agency links (LatAm/APAC volume, gap 7) and macro vintage sources (gap 4) not yet in our FRED/Eurostat/BEA holdings; needs a section-by-section read to confirm specifics.

candidates.name: awesome-economics (brandonhimpfen)
candidates.what_it_holds: Smaller (15-star) curated list explicitly of datasets, tools, models, and institutions for economics, updated 6 Sep 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent economics-data index to cross-check against gap 4 (vintage/ALFRED-style data) and gap 6 (consumer spend panels); not yet inspected section-by-section.

candidates.name: awesome-quant
candidates.what_it_holds: 29.5k-star flagship quant-finance resource list, updated same-day. Confirmed sections: Alternative Data & Sentiment (news/social sentiment tools), Economic & Macro Data (OmniOracle: 500+ series from FRED/World Bank/EIA/NOAA; pystlouisfed and fedfred: Python clients for FRED, ALFRED, GeoFRED and FRASER -- i.e. vintage/point-in-time macro data; treasurydirect, treasury-fiscaldata, newyorkfed, commitments-of-traders TypeScript API clients; estat-mcp for Japanese e-Stat data), Point-in-Time & Vintage Data Tools (ashare-data-immunity, pit-adjuster -- China A-share point-in-time adjustment, not US-relevant), and Institutional/Corporate Filings (edgartools, SECfinAPI, edinetdb/edinet-mcp for Japanese XBRL filings).
candidates.why_useful: pystlouisfed / fedfred give a maintained Python client to FRED's ALFRED (archival vintage) service, which is exactly the 'ALFRED-style macro vintages' asked for in gap 4; estat-mcp is a ready client for Japanese government statistics (GDP/CPI/trade) relevant to gap 7 APAC volume.
candidates.size_hint: README index; linked clients are small pip/npm packages
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: FRED is already held (non-vintage); ALFRED vintages via pystlouisfed/fedfred would be new

candidates.name: awesome-quant (thuquant, Chinese)
candidates.what_it_holds: 5,623-star Chinese-language index of quant resources, updated same-day; not inspected section-by-section in this pass.
candidates.why_useful: Possible route to Chinese short-term-rental/travel platform data clients (Tujia, Xiaozhu -- gap 9) or China-specific macro/travel statistics; unconfirmed, flagged for a future Chinese-language-capable pass.

candidates.name: awesome-transportation-network-data
candidates.what_it_holds: 18-star curated list of transportation-network test datasets: TNTP (Sioux Falls, Anaheim, Barcelona, Chicago network-equilibrium data), Hazmat (Buffalo/Albany hazardous-materials routing + accident data), Korean Expressway EV-charging origin-destination flows, DC-NY-Boston corridor EV network, Eastern Massachusetts traffic-assignment network with observed traffic counts, Pisa OR-Group optimization instances; also points to a sibling 'Awesome-Transit' list (transit APIs/datasets) and VRP-REP (vehicle-routing datasets).
candidates.why_useful: Mostly academic network-equilibrium/routing test data, not real-world passenger volumes -- low direct value for ABNB nights/travel demand, but the linked Awesome-Transit could hold public transit passenger datasets relevant to gap 10 (transport capacity/traffic); worth a follow-up fetch of that sibling list specifically.
candidates.size_hint: handful of small academic network files
candidates.geography: US (Sioux Falls, Buffalo/Albany, DC-NY-Boston, Massachusetts), South Korea, Italy (Pisa)
candidates.time_coverage: static benchmark networks, no time series

candidates.name: awesome-transportation
candidates.what_it_holds: 0-star, very recently created (4 Sep 2026) curated list claiming 'tools, datasets, standards, and learning resources for transportation and mobility'; contents not verified in this pass.
candidates.why_useful: Too new/unverified to rate confidently; flagged only because its description explicitly promises datasets for mobility, which overlaps gap 10.

notes: Literal 'awesome-tourism-data' and 'awesome-real-estate-data' and 'awesome-transportation-data' repos as named in the theme hint do not exist on GitHub -- searches for those exact multi-word phrases returned zero results, and broader single/double-word variants (awesome-tourism, awesome-transportation) surfaced mostly unrelated app boilerplate or academic network-equilibrium data rather than travel-demand/STR data. The awesome-public-datasets family is dominated by dozens of near-identical forks/clones of the same list (0-15 stars each) not worth cataloguing individually; only the canonical awesomedata/awesome-public-datasets and its apd-core backing repo are listed. WebSearch quota was exhausted session-wide before I could do a broader non-gh search for tourism-specific curated lists -- a follow-up scout with search budget remaining could usefully retry 'awesome tourism dataset github' and 'awesome hospitality data github'. Best concrete new leads from this pass: pystlouisfed/fedfred (ALFRED vintage macro data, gap 4), HM Land Registry + Dubai Pulse (free point-in-time property transactions, gap 13), and Staying API (live Airbnb/STR pricing via free tier, gap 2) -- all reached via awesome-list pointers rather than being awesome-lists themselves, so the awesome lists functioned mainly as a discovery layer rather than holding data directly. No repo in this theme should be treated as high potential on its own merits; the value is in what they point to.
